newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian space probe stuck in earth's orbit.
newsitem.headline: Russian space probe stuck in earth's orbit.

text.p: A Russian space probe launched on a mission to Mars ran into problems after liftoff and was unable to leave the earth's orbit, a Russian Space Agency spokesman said on Sunday.
"We've got a problem. The probe had been due leave the earth's orbit last night but it is still there. We are trying to sort it out," Vladimir Ananyev told Reuters.
The six-tonne probe, which lifted off from Kazakhstan's Baikonur space centre on Saturday at 11.48 p.m. Moscow time (2048 GMT), was due to reach Mars on September 12 next year.
Ananyev said repairs were under way. "There is a chance the repairs will be successful, but it's too early to say how the situation will develop."

The $64 million Russian mission is the second of three planned trips from Earth to Mars in just over a month. The United States launched one robot voyage to the Red Planet two weeks ago and a second mission will blast off on December 2.
All will check for signs of water on the far-away planet -- a key clue to whether there was once life on Mars.
